text.p: Programme of matches in the French
first division this weekend (standings in parentheses, all
kick-off times GMT):
Saturday:
Auxerre (7) v Rennes (16) 1800
League top scorer Stephane Guivarc'h plays at Auxerre for the
first time since joining Rennes from the reigning champions this
weekend. Auxerre need a win to stay in line for a UEFA Cup
place, while Rennes are still without an away win.
Metz (5) v Bastia (8) 1800
Corsicans Bastia, a point behind in-form fifth-placed Metz and
-- at eighth -- out of the automatic UEFA Cup places, will be
looking to get back in the frame with a first win in five
matches.
Le Havre (15) v Nice (20) 1800
Bottom club Nice, their minds on the French Cup final next
weekend, should be easy meat for Le Havre who can ensure safety
from relegation with a victory.
Lyon (9) v Lille (18) 1800
Lille's confidence has been damaged by six defeats in row which
have dropped the club into relegation zone, while Lyon's run of
six wins in seven games has lifted them close to UEFA Cup
qualification.
Paris St Germain (2) v Bordeaux (4) 1800
Bordeaux, currently fourth, are the first of a trio of strong
rivals for PSG in their last three games. PSG will be looking to
hang on to second place and qualify for the European Cup.
Lens (13) v Marseille (11) 1800
Penultimate chance for Marseille to avoid ending the season
without an away victory, while one point should be enough for
Lens to ensure they avoid relegation.
Guingamp (12) v Nantes (3) 1800
Nantes should extend their unbeaten run to 29 matches against a
side depleted by injuries and looking to field a fully fit squad
in next weekend's French Cup final. Nantes defender Eric Decroix
is still out with injury.
Montpellier (10) v Nancy (17) 1800
Nancy, six points under the relegation zone cut-off with only
nine points left to play for, cannot afford even to draw against
a mid-table Montpellier who have an outside chance of a place in
the Intertoto Cup.
Sunday:
Cannes (14) v Strasbourg (6) 1630
Cannes need three more points to guarantee survival in the top
flight. Strasbourg, in the UEFA Cup as League Cup winners, have
lost three of their last four games.
Monaco (1) v Caen (19) 1830
If PSG drop points against Bordeaux, Monaco can celebrate the
title on Saturday. Otherwise, champagne bottles will be kept on
ice waiting for Monaco to secure their sixth championship at
Stade Louis II by taking at least one point from this clash.
